target: Spoiler-free maximum verifiable completion of the original Japanese Biohazard 5Z cabinet

areas.name: Archival Cabinet Route
areas.location_cue: The Biohazard 5Z model plate, reel window, main screen, movable subdisplay, buttons, lamps, and operator panel.
areas.note: All guidance assumes a lawfully owned private cabinet in non-wager free play.

save_backup.title: Back up the starting cabinet state
save_backup.why: Service changes and persistent counters can alter the only reproducible setup.
save_backup.detail: Photograph every accessible setting and counter, preserve firmware information, and record a full power-on test before play.

levels.1: The selected catalog entry is an amusement machine, not the campaign game.
levels.2: Use an authentic Japanese Biohazard 5Z pachislot cabinet.
levels.3: Verify the model plate, Enterrise branding, 2012 machine record, original reels, main screen, movable subdisplay, control panel, and cabinet firmware before recording any completion evidence.

levels.1: The moving secondary display is part of the original presentation.
levels.2: Confirm the movable subdisplay operates with the main screen and reels.
levels.3: Record a synchronized test showing reel spin, button lamps, main display, subdisplay movement, cabinet lighting, speakers, and control response. Do not substitute a static video capture for cabinet-specific effects.

levels.1: Archival completion does not require gambling.
levels.2: Configure the lawfully owned cabinet for private, non-wager free play.
levels.3: Use only an authorized owner or technician and the original operator documentation. Do not deposit money, seek payouts, evade local law, or alter certified hardware merely to trigger a checklist entry.

levels.1: Configuration changes belong to the cabinet owner.
levels.2: Use the service controls only with owner authorization.
levels.3: Power down when the operator manual requires it, photograph the original setting before changes, log every service adjustment, and restore the starting configuration after the archival session. Unsupported button sequences remain withheld.

levels.1: Important cues can appear on several surfaces at once.
levels.2: Frame the reels, buttons, main screen, subdisplay, lamps, and audio together.
levels.3: Begin recording before power-on and retain an uncut native-audio master. Add a separate close view only when it remains time-synchronized, so a reel result cannot be paired accidentally with the wrong display effect.

levels.1: Counters and service settings may affect a long session.
levels.2: Photograph all legally accessible counters and configuration screens before play.
levels.3: Record cabinet model, firmware, configuration, credit state, visible counters, free-play hardware, date, and power-cycle status. Preserve the images before any reset or test because persistent-memory behavior is not fully documented.

levels.1: A later software reproduction exists outside the chosen catalog route.
levels.2: Keep mobile-application footage separate from cabinet completion.
levels.3: Use the application only as clearly labeled historical comparison if it is lawfully preserved. Its practice features, automation, timing, and presentation do not replace evidence captured from the original cabinet.

areas.name: Reel Controls and Visible Roles
areas.location_cue: The lever, three stop buttons, reel window, navigation lamps, credit display, and symbol-result response.
areas.note: The pack records safe cabinet operation and observable roles without supplying wagering strategy.

save_backup.title: Preserve a clean control baseline
save_backup.why: A wrong stop order may cause an undocumented penalty.
save_backup.detail: Record several permitted free-play spins and confirm all buttons, lamps, reels, and navigation cues before attempting rare states.

levels.1: Normal play begins by watching one symbol on the left reel.
levels.2: Aim for the cherry symbol on the left reel first.
levels.3: Start each ordinary spin with the left reel, stop near the cherry symbol, then inspect its final position before choosing the remaining reel procedure. Use a cabinet-level close capture to verify the stop pattern.

levels.1: A corner stop changes what to watch next.
levels.2: When a cherry stops at the corner, aim for cherries on the middle and right reels.
levels.3: Keep the permitted normal stop order, target the matching symbols on both remaining reels, and record the completed line. Do not assign a role strength unless the final combination is visible.

levels.1: A centered cherry uses the simpler remaining procedure.
levels.2: When the cherry stops in the middle, stop the other reels without a special target.
levels.3: Complete the spin in an allowed order, capture all three final reel positions, and log the accompanying screen and lamp response. Preserve the result before interpreting it as a chance role.

levels.1: Another left-reel stop requires matching symbols.
levels.2: When the watermelon symbol appears in its target position, aim for watermelons on both remaining reels.
levels.3: Hold the camera on the entire reel window, stop the middle and right reels on the matching symbol, and record the final alignment plus any display response. Missed visual timing must not be counted as the role.

levels.1: Ordinary play restricts reel order.
levels.2: Use left-to-right stopping or the documented sandwich order during normal play.
levels.3: Begin with the left reel, then use either middle followed by right or right followed by middle. Follow a displayed navigation order instead whenever the cabinet supplies one.

levels.1: An unsupported reel order can change the machine state.
levels.2: Do not begin normal spins from the middle or right reel.
levels.3: Use only the two documented normal orders unless an on-screen navigation cue overrides them. If an accidental order occurs, record it and stop the session until the original manual establishes the consequence.

levels.1: The cabinet sometimes supplies a specific stop sequence.
levels.2: During Hazard Rush, obey the illuminated or displayed reel order.
levels.3: Read the complete navigation cue before pressing a stop button, follow its sequence exactly, and capture both the cue and final symbols. Return to the ordinary procedure only after navigation disappears.

levels.1: This symbol result belongs in the cabinet role ledger.
levels.2: Capture a complete reel stop showing Red 7.
levels.3: Record the spin from lever input through final reel positions, payout or replay response, and every simultaneous display cue. Catalogue Red 7 as replay plus ART, while leaving unverified probability and hidden-state effects out of the player-facing instructions.

levels.3: Record the spin from lever input through final reel positions, payout or replay response, and every simultaneous display cue. Catalogue BAR as Shooting Burst replay, while leaving unverified probability and hidden-state effects out of the player-facing instructions.

areas.name: Normal States and Physical Cues
areas.location_cue: Ordinary-play backgrounds, transition effects, stage captions, payline flashes, and the movable status display.
areas.note: Locations are described only by physical appearance; hidden-state claims remain evidence-based.

save_backup.title: Save the initial state record
save_backup.why: Power cycling or service changes may alter counters and hidden conditions.
save_backup.detail: Preserve the untouched opening sequence and cabinet settings before comparing state cues.

levels.1: Normal play can use a hidden chance level.
levels.2: Log visible cues that are consistent with low internal state.
levels.3: Record the physical stage, transition effect, bell-line response, caption position, recent role history, and next chance-zone result. Treat the state as an inference unless a service display or repeated evidence confirms it.

levels.1: Normal play can use a hidden chance level.
levels.2: Log visible cues that are consistent with normal internal state.
levels.3: Record the physical stage, transition effect, bell-line response, caption position, recent role history, and next chance-zone result. Treat the state as an inference unless a service display or repeated evidence confirms it.

levels.2: Log visible cues that are consistent with high internal state.
levels.3: Record the physical stage, transition effect, bell-line response, caption position, recent role history, and next chance-zone result. Treat the state as an inference unless a service display or repeated evidence confirms it.

levels.3: Record the physical stage, transition effect, bell-line response, caption position, recent role history, and next chance-zone result. Treat the state as an inference unless a service display or repeated evidence confirms it.

levels.1: The hidden state changes access likelihood rather than reel controls.
levels.2: Compare chance-zone entries across different visible state cues.
levels.3: Keep configuration and play procedure fixed, log each qualifying role and subsequent zone entry, and compare only after a large direct-capture sample. Do not present an exact transition rate without verified data.

levels.1: The hidden level does not immediately fall during ordinary play.
levels.2: Track the same inferred state until a chance zone or Hazard Rush begins.
levels.3: Continue logging cues without declaring a downgrade from one quiet spin. End the state segment when a documented major entry occurs, then begin a new inference record afterward.

levels.1: A colored stage change can indicate stronger conditions.
levels.2: Capture a stage transition surrounded by red effects.
levels.3: Record the screen before, during, and after the transition, then follow the next roles and zone entries. Catalogue it as a high-state cue, not a guaranteed award.

levels.1: A normal payout can carry an extra visual signal.
levels.2: Capture a bell result whose winning line flashes.
levels.3: Keep the entire reel result and payline visible, record subsequent play without cutting, and catalogue the flash as a high-state cue. Do not confuse it with the ordinary bell animation.

levels.1: A location label can appear on the opposite side.
levels.2: Capture the stage name displayed at the upper right instead of the usual upper left.
levels.3: Record the preceding transition and every following spin until the next zone, Rush entry, or clear return to ordinary play. Treat the reversed placement as a prelude cue rather than a guaranteed result.

levels.2: Capture a complete visit to the public gathering area.
levels.3: Begin with the incoming transition, preserve the main and movable displays, record every ordinary animation or role response encountered there, and keep narrative interpretation out of the guide.

areas.name: Hazard Rush Entry Zones
areas.location_cue: The dedicated mission or percentage screen reached from ordinary play before the main Rush mode.
areas.note: Mode names that expose identities are replaced with neutral mechanical labels.

save_backup.title: Preserve the normal-play lead-in
save_backup.why: A chance zone may end quickly or return after a hidden delay.
save_backup.detail: Record continuously from the triggering role through the final success, failure, or delayed re-entry.

levels.1: One normal-play transition offers a separate route into Hazard Rush.
levels.2: Enter Elimination Mission and complete its displayed objective.
levels.3: Reach it through special elimination replay; it lasts twenty games. Follow the displayed reel navigation and defeat displayed target count. Record every draw, counter change, success or failure screen, and any delayed re-entry; the published success estimate is over fifty percent.

levels.1: One normal-play transition offers a separate route into Hazard Rush.
levels.2: Enter Encirclement Zone and complete its displayed objective.
levels.3: Reach it through selected chance roles; it lasts ten twenty thirty or continuing. Follow the displayed reel navigation and clear surrounding targets. Record every draw, counter change, success or failure screen, and any delayed re-entry; the published success estimate is about thirty-five percent.

levels.1: One normal-play transition offers a separate route into Hazard Rush.
levels.2: Enter Rank-Up Zone and complete its displayed objective.
levels.3: Reach it through selected chance roles; it lasts about twenty to thirty. Follow the displayed reel navigation and raise movable-display percentage. Record every draw, counter change, success or failure screen, and any delayed re-entry; the published success estimate is over sixty percent.

areas.name: Hazard Rush
areas.location_cue: The red-symbol entry, Four-Reel Challenge, active game counter, navigation prompts, and addition animations.
areas.note: Credit figures are cabinet specifications and observations, never wagering promises.

save_backup.title: Preserve the complete Rush entry
save_backup.why: Rare additions and transformations can occur without warning.
save_backup.detail: Record continuously from the triggering result until Hazard Rush and any immediate recovery mode have fully ended.

levels.1: The main mode can begin through more than one mechanical route.
levels.2: Capture one direct or prelude entry and each neutral chance-zone entry.
levels.3: Index the triggering role, preceding state cues, zone result when applicable, red-symbol alignment, and first Rush frame. Keep separate evidence for each verified route instead of treating one entry as universal.

levels.1: The main counter begins within a documented range.
levels.2: Capture a Hazard Rush start between 50 and 300 games.
levels.3: Record the complete Four-Reel Challenge, every symbol line, the final awarded counter, and the first decrementing Rush frame. Do not combine values from different starts.

levels.1: The mode has a documented average machine rate.
levels.2: Log the cabinet's credit change across a clean Hazard Rush sample.
levels.3: Record starting credits, games played, visible payouts, navigation accuracy, and ending credits. Compare the direct result with the documented approximate 2.3-credit-per-game specification without presenting it as a guaranteed return.

levels.1: Reel prompts take priority inside the main mode.
levels.2: Follow every displayed reel-order instruction during Hazard Rush.
levels.3: Wait for the full cue, press the stop buttons in the shown order, and retain both the navigation and stopped reels in one frame. Log any missed instruction separately instead of counting the affected spin.

levels.1: The opening symbol arrangement sets the starting counter.
levels.2: Align the red symbols on the main reels and movable display.
levels.3: Follow the displayed aiming prompt, capture the main and subdisplay alignments together, and record the resulting counter. A four-symbol single line awards 100 games; a double line awards 200 or 300.

levels.1: Chance roles can extend the active counter.
levels.2: Capture a role that adds games during Hazard Rush.
levels.3: Record the role, existing counter, raw award, any later transformation, and final total before the counter resumes. Keep the direct award separate from Growth or Mutation.

levels.1: An awarded number can multiply after appearing.
levels.2: Capture an addition that enters the Growth animation.
levels.3: Record the original number, each color stage, every multiplication step, and the final counter. Growth can reach a 27-times result; do not stop recording after the first increase.

levels.1: The first multiplication stage has a blue background.
levels.2: Capture blue behind an active Growth sequence.
levels.3: Keep the initial award and next transformation in the same recording, then mark blue as the first visible stage rather than a final multiplier guarantee.

levels.1: A later multiplication stage changes the background to green.
levels.2: Capture green during the same Growth chain.
levels.3: Record the number entering green, any additional multiplication, and the final counter. Catalogue green as the second visible stage without inferring its probability.

levels.1: The deepest documented color stage uses red.
levels.2: Capture red before the Growth result settles.
levels.3: Preserve every earlier stage and the final multiplied award in one sequence. Catalogue red as the third visible stage and retain the exact observed multiplier.

levels.1: An award can change form instead of multiplying conventionally.
levels.2: Capture a displayed game award that mutates into a larger number.
levels.3: Record the original award, the visual distortion, each intermediate display, and the final counter addition. Keep Mutation separate from Growth in the session index.

areas.name: Special Addition Modes
areas.location_cue: The Burst weapon screen, changing background, infected main display, distorted reels, and nested mode transitions.
areas.note: Identity-bearing mode names are reduced to neutral mechanical descriptions.

save_backup.title: Keep the entire nested sequence
save_backup.why: Infection, Burst, Growth, Mutation, and Interludes can overlap.
save_backup.detail: Record without cuts from the first altered display until every nested mode has returned to ordinary Hazard Rush.

levels.1: This specialized addition mode has a distinct observable pattern.
levels.2: Align BAR during the displayed cut-in.
levels.3: Capture the cut-in, BAR result, mode title, starting background, and first added value.

levels.1: This specialized addition mode has a distinct observable pattern.
levels.2: Continue free-play spins inside Burst.
levels.3: Record each stopped role and its addition until the continuation check ends the mode.

levels.1: This specialized addition mode has a distinct observable pattern.
levels.2: Keep playing until Burst declines continuation.
levels.3: Capture every retained round and the exact final transition back to Hazard Rush.

levels.1: This specialized addition mode has a distinct observable pattern.
levels.2: Press the chance button on the Burst entry screen.
levels.3: Record the resulting background and catalogue the documented order from white through rainbow.

levels.1: This specialized addition mode has a distinct observable pattern.
levels.2: Reach Burst with the baseline handgun display.
levels.3: Capture its award, continuation result, and any later Growth or Mutation.

levels.1: This specialized addition mode has a distinct observable pattern.
levels.2: Reach Burst with the baseline shotgun display.
levels.3: Capture its award, continuation result, and any later Growth or Mutation.

levels.1: This specialized addition mode has a distinct observable pattern.
levels.2: Reach Burst with the gatling display.
levels.3: Record the complete attack and verify an addition of at least 20 games.

levels.1: This specialized addition mode has a distinct observable pattern.
levels.2: Reach Burst with the helper attack.
levels.3: Record the full cameo attack and verify an addition of at least 30 games without naming the character.

levels.1: This specialized addition mode has a distinct observable pattern.
levels.2: Reach Burst with the rocket display.
levels.3: Record the launch and verify an addition of at least 50 games.

levels.1: This specialized addition mode has a distinct observable pattern.
levels.2: Reach Burst with a weapon other than handgun or shotgun.
levels.3: Capture the weapon, award, and next continuation result; treat it as a strong continuation cue.

levels.1: The infected display changes addition opportunities.
levels.2: Capture the screen becoming visibly infected.
levels.3: Record its entry context, main and subdisplay changes, first qualifying role, and later exit.

levels.1: The infected display changes addition opportunities.
levels.2: Log roles throughout the infected interval.
levels.3: Count direct stopped results and compare them with ordinary footage; retain the documented approximate fivefold rate as a specification.

levels.1: The infected display changes addition opportunities.
levels.2: Continue until Burst or an Interlude begins.
levels.3: Capture the complete transition and the infected display that immediately preceded it.

levels.1: The infected display changes addition opportunities.
levels.2: Enter Burst while Infection remains active.
levels.3: Record each added value and compare the direct session result with the documented approximate doubling.

levels.1: The infected display changes addition opportunities.
levels.2: Enter an Interlude while Infection remains active.
levels.3: Record chance-role additions and compare the direct session result with the documented approximate twentyfold effect.

levels.1: The infected display changes addition opportunities.
levels.2: Remain in Burst or an Interlude until it ends.
levels.3: Capture that the infected presentation persists throughout the nested mode and record when it finally clears.

areas.name: Interludes, Premium Mode, and Recovery
areas.location_cue: The paused Rush counter, neutral interlude presentation, premium identifier, door-button sequence, tablet counter, and recovery exit.
areas.note: Narrative images are indexed without titles, identities, ordering, or outcomes.

save_backup.title: Preserve the Rush state before rare transitions
save_backup.why: Interludes and recovery results can alter a long, difficult-to-reproduce session.
save_backup.detail: Keep a synchronized counter log and uninterrupted recording from before entry until ordinary Hazard Rush or normal play resumes.

levels.1: A chance role during Hazard Rush can pause the main counter.
levels.2: Capture the transition into a story interlude.
levels.3: Record the triggering role, remaining Rush games, transition, interlude counter, and first frame. Do not describe the narrative content or identify characters.

levels.1: The internal pseudo-bonus uses one of two documented lengths.
levels.2: Capture an interlude lasting 20 or 40 games.
levels.3: Count from the first playable interlude game through its exit, record the selected length, and verify that the main Hazard Rush counter remains unchanged.

levels.1: The main game allowance is protected during the interlude.
levels.2: Compare the Hazard Rush counter immediately before and after the interlude.
levels.3: Keep both counter values and the complete interlude in one capture. Separate any added games from the unchanged pre-existing counter when reconciling the result.

levels.1: Chance roles can still extend the main mode here.
levels.2: Capture a game addition during an interlude.
levels.3: Record the stopped role, raw addition, Infection status, Growth or Mutation, and final Hazard Rush total before the interlude ends.

levels.1: The internal sequence contains several separate presentation slots.
levels.2: Fill every interlude slot exposed by the cabinet's own sequence or index.
levels.3: Capture each distinct slot from its opening frame through its return to play, label it only by neutral capture order, and verify the collection against the cabinet rather than exposing titles, plot order, or narrative outcomes.

levels.1: A rare main-mode variant protects the counter until an interlude.
levels.2: Capture the premium Hazard Rush presentation.
levels.3: Record the complete entry, visible premium identifier, active counter, and every spin until the next interlude. Verify that the existing counter does not decrease during this interval.

levels.1: The premium state can return after an interlude.
levels.2: Complete the displayed button sequence after the interlude.
levels.3: Press only when prompted, record the door-destruction animation, and continue through the resulting screen. Count a return only when the cabinet visibly restores the premium state.

levels.1: Zero remaining Rush games opens one recovery opportunity.
levels.2: Let the Hazard Rush counter reach zero and capture the recovery-zone transition.
levels.3: Record the final decrement, entry screen, tablet counter, and every stopped role. Preserve a backup or reproducible free-play state before intentionally testing expiration.

levels.1: Collectible tablets can restore Hazard Rush.
levels.2: Accumulate six tablets before the falling replay ends the opportunity.
levels.3: Record every tablet award, its triggering role, the counter reaching six, and the full return to Hazard Rush. Do not combine tablets from separate recovery attempts.

levels.1: One replay result ends an unsuccessful recovery attempt.
levels.2: Capture the falling-replay result before six tablets are collected.
levels.3: Record the reel result, remaining tablet count, exit animation, and next cabinet state. Use a separate copied setup for this failure capture if the cabinet's counters cannot be restored safely.

areas.note: Configuration data is preserved as machine documentation, not as betting advice.

save_backup.title: Save the original operator setting
save_backup.why: Changing configuration can invalidate every comparison and may affect persistent counters.
save_backup.detail: Photograph the starting value, use only authorized service access, and restore it after each isolated free-play sample.

areas.note: Every publicly documented rare effect is represented; a separate hold covers the unknown complete cabinet catalogue.

save_backup.title: Preserve every first occurrence
save_backup.why: Many effects are stochastic and may never repeat on the surviving cabinet.
save_backup.detail: Keep the first uncut capture, note configuration and mode, then duplicate it before continuing the session.

areas.name: Final Archival Audit
areas.location_cue: The cabinet provenance file, synchronized footage, role ledger, mode timeline, configuration records, presentation index, and verification holds.
areas.note: Completion means every documented mechanical and presentation element plus an honest record of what surviving evidence cannot establish.

save_backup.title: Duplicate the completed archive
save_backup.why: The final evidence combines rare stochastic events and irreplaceable cabinet records.
save_backup.detail: Keep two checked copies of raw footage, photographs, operator notes, translations, configuration logs, and the final checklist before reconciliation.

levels.1: The final archive must prove the selected machine route.
levels.2: Confirm model, manufacturer, cabinet, firmware, free-play setup, and original configuration.
levels.3: Compare the model plate, cabinet photographs, synchronized power-on recording, service record, and backup checksums. Reject application-only or unidentified video evidence.

levels.1: Every safe procedure and visible role needs a complete reel capture.
levels.2: Confirm the permitted stop orders, navigation, follow-up aiming, and all catalogued symbols.
levels.3: Review each recording from lever input through final reels and display response. Mark accidental penalty-risk spins separately and leave unsupported combination meanings unresolved.

levels.1: Each route into the main mode has a separate objective.
levels.2: Confirm complete success and failure evidence for every neutral chance zone.
levels.3: Verify the trigger, counter or percentage display, reel inputs, objective, terminal screen, delayed return, and resulting cabinet state for each mode.

levels.1: The main mode contains several addition systems.
levels.2: Confirm entry, Four-Reel Challenge, navigation, direct addition, Growth, and Mutation.
levels.3: Reconcile the original counter, each raw award, every multiplication or mutation, and the final counter. Keep nominal credit-rate testing separate from completion evidence.

levels.1: Nested modes require synchronized evidence.
levels.2: Confirm Burst patterns, Infection effects, interludes, Premium mode, and recovery.
levels.3: Use the mode timeline to verify entry, protected counters, additions, nested persistence, return conditions, tablet recovery, and the falling-replay exit without exposing narrative content.

levels.1: Operator-level comparisons must remain isolated and reversible.
levels.2: Confirm every documented configuration and the restored original setting.
levels.3: Review authorization, before-and-after photographs, published specification values, free-play samples, and restoration evidence. Exclude any session involving wagering.

levels.1: Rare effects and physical scenes need indexed first-occurrence captures.
levels.2: Confirm every represented rare effect, Easter egg, and presentation scene.
levels.3: Open the capture index and verify each entry includes lead-in, full event, immediate result, next playable state, configuration, and mode. Keep the complete-catalogue hold unresolved unless original documentation closes it.

levels.1: Maximum verifiable completion must retain its unknown boundaries.
levels.2: Review every hold and attach repeatable cabinet evidence to resolved entries.
levels.3: Leave unsupported holds uncertain. Replace one only after lawful hardware or original documentation establishes the exact detail, and list all remaining holds in the report.
